questions.question: What is the purpose of composing seven surfaces?
options: Make the full reliability contract explicit
Hide all of the harness's controls
Remove the independent review step
Automate the whole production deployment now
questions.explanation: Composition connects the mechanisms while keeping ownership visible.

questions.question: What does the harness control plane do?
options: Write arbitrary files to production
Replace the underlying model entirely
Evaluate evidence and route readiness
Delete receipts from failed checks
questions.explanation: The control plane governs decisions around the model.

questions.question: When is a report ready in this project?
options: When the maker's note simply sounds confident
When exactly one test happens to pass
When the candidate diff is simply large
When scope, feedback, checks, and review pass

questions.question: What should a blocked handoff contain?
options: No context at all about what happened
The failed surface and next repair action
A success claim offered with no real evidence
A fully hidden, unrecorded exception
questions.explanation: A blocked state must preserve actionable context.

questions.question: Why keep instructions as a separate field?
options: To count the words used in the prompt
To avoid persisting any durable state
To fully replace the scope contract instead
To prove which startup rules were loaded
questions.explanation: Surface ownership remains reviewable when it is explicit.

questions.question: What should happen after a ready report?
options: An irreversible deploy that runs automatically
Erasing the report once it is marked ready
Human approval or the configured next gate
Skipping the handoff to the next session
questions.explanation: Readiness is evidence for the next gate, not permission for every side effect.
